title: Proportional token differentials and enterprise commit variants
creator: Amira Patel
description: Goal: Run a controlled experiment for per-token pricing that distinguishes input vs output tokens, applies streaming-adjacent price modifiers, and evaluates several minimum-commit (enterprise commit) variants to find the best trade-off between unit economics and conversion for mid-market & enterprise signups. Also validate that pricing variants map cleanly to enterprise security questionnaire / contract terms without widening legal friction.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Experiment infra captures token-level input/output counts (non-streaming and streaming) and attributes revenue to buckets by cohort.
2) Run two parallel cohorts (control = current flat per-token rate; treatment groups = proportional IO split, streaming step-down, and two commit levels).
3) Statistically significant lift in conversion or revenue-per-customer (p<0.05) for at least one treatment without >5% churn increase on high-usage customers.
4) Legal & Security confirm that the commit variants map to existing contract templates or provide required questionnaire responses with <=2 additional clauses.
5) Console shows clear cost/latency examples for each variant in the billing explainer page.
experiment_design:
Hypotheses:
- H1: Charging lower per-token for inputs (where applicable) and slightly higher for outputs better aligns costs with compute and will not materially harm revenue; it increases perceived fairness for customers using embeddings/prediction-heavy workloads.
- H2: Streaming requests introduce operational overhead; applying a small streaming surcharge for sub-second streaming or offering a streaming-discount band (step-down after threshold) reduces extreme tail costs while improving adoption for low-volume streaming users.
- H3: Offering two enterprise commit variants (Commit-A: lower per-token with 6-month commit; Commit-B: deeper discount with 12-month commit + basic support) will increase average contract size without creating additional legal burden if mapped to existing PLAs and SOW templates.
cohorts_and_allocation:
- Control: current flat per-token price for both input/output and streaming. (30% traffic)
- Treatment 1 (IO-split): separate input rate = 0.6x base, output rate = 1.15x base; streaming same as non-streaming. (20% traffic)
- Treatment 2 (Streaming-step): flat per-token but streaming surcharge 10% up to 1M tokens/month, then 5% discount beyond threshold. (20% traffic)
- Treatment 3 (Commit-A): 6-month enterprise commit: 15% discount on combined IO rates + 1 dedicated onboarding credit. (15% traffic, invite-only)
- Treatment 4 (Commit-B): 12-month enterprise commit: 25% discount + phone support + quarterly review. (15% traffic, sales-led)
Cohort segmentation: by historical monthly spend buckets (S: < $500/mo, M: $500–5k, L: > $5k), and by product usage (chat vs embeddings vs rerank).
metrics:
Primary: conversion rate for free->paid, ARR per customer, revenue per token, churn rate at 30 & 90 days.
Secondary: average latency (to detect regressions from streaming policy), support ticket volume per cohort, legal review time for contracts, number of deals requiring custom paperwork.
Instrumentation: token-level counters, streaming session IDs, cohort tags in billing events, A/B test id in request headers. Dashboards to be created in Console: pricing-experiment/PM-9840 with daily and hourly granularity.

notes:
Trade-offs discussed: simple flat price is easy to explain but misprices workloads dominated by input tokens (e.g., embeddings). IO-splitting increases bill complexity; we will prioritize clear billing examples and SDK helpers to calculate estimated monthly spend. Streaming-step approach chosen over per-second billing due to telemetry constraints and high variance in session lengths.
Open question: whether to surface a streaming surcharge on the dashboard as a separate line item or fold into base per-token rate for clarity. Preference from Growth is a separate line item for transparency; Finance prefers aggregated rate to simplify invoices.
